item.title: align the evaluate tool with [component] 1.14 and OpenRouter refusals
item.body:
## Summary

[component] moved `[component]-latest` to [component] 1.14 (`[component]-1.14.0`) on 2026-10-14, and OpenRouter's Decisions API added a refusal answer. This brings the `evaluate` server in line with both.

- **Box on `[component]-latest`.** The local box gate still treated `[component]-latest` as [component] 1.13 and refused it. It now refuses only the 1.13 ids (`[component]-1.13.0`, `[component]-1.13`, and the OpenRouter 1.13 ids). Both backend defaults are now 1.14, so the fallback no longer needs a pinned box model: `ProviderSpec.BoxModel` and the fallback's model swap are removed.
- **Refusals pass through.** OpenRouter answers `{"type":"refusal"}` when a provider declines one question. That used to fail the whole call as a type mismatch. A refusal is now accepted as that question's answer, with no value filled in, and the other answers come back normally. A refusal that also carries a value is rejected. The OpenRouter backend note tells the agent to treat a refusal as no judgment, never as a "no".
- **Guidance.** Following [component]'s skill 0.6.2, the server instructions suggest a companion `noul` ("does anything fit?") over a no-match option when nothing may fit.
- **Contract doc.** [path omitted] records the 2026-11-14 fetches of both OpenAPI documents: OpenRouter's top-level `assets` map (accepted there; this server keeps sending `image_url` by design), the refusal answer, an optional `noul` confidence on OpenRouter, and [component]'s nullable box confidence.

item.title: keep harm-halt clear tokens off the terminal when a test file runs on its own
item.body:
# Keep harm-halt clear tokens off the terminal when a test file runs on its own

## What changes

Running one test file directly, for example [path omitted], printed harm-halt clear tokens on the developer's terminal. The tokens belong to the throwaway repos the tests create, so no real halt was involved. They still flooded the terminal of whoever started the session.

The only guard was `COMPONENT_HARM_HALT_TERMINAL=off` in `suite_child_env.child_environment`, which applies only when the suite dispatchers start a test. Now:

- `suite_child_env` holds the switch and its value in one place (`HARM_HALT_TERMINAL`), and gains `withhold_harm_halt_tokens()`, which sets it for the current process and every child it starts.
- `run_counted`, which every unit test's `__main__` goes through, calls it first. A test file run on its own now behaves like one the suite started.
- The tests that show the token on a fake terminal (`OwnerTerminalCase`) still clear the switch for each test, so the real terminal path stays covered.
